chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I was with him when a man came and asked him. He said: 'A man divorced his wife three times.' He said: 'She becomes permanently divorced from him.' The man left, then another of our companions came and asked: 'A man divorced his wife three times.' He said: 'One divorce.' Another came and asked: 'A man divorced his wife three times.' He said: 'It is nothing (no effect).' Then he looked at me and said: 'It is as you see.' I said: 'How is this?' He said: 'This one believes that if a man divorces his wife three times, she becomes permanently divorced from him. And I believe that if a man divorces his wife three times in accordance with the Sunnah, she becomes permanently divorced from him. And if a man divorces his wife three times while she is in a state of purity, it is only one divorce. And if a man divorces his wife three times while she is not in a state of purity, it is nothing (no effect).'

key_terms.بَانَتْ مِنْهُ: she becomes permanently divorced from him
key_terms.عَلَى غَيْرِ طُهُورٍ: not in a state of purity

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on triple divorce pronounced together in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar highlights the foundational Shia doctrine of *Talaq al-Sunnah* (divorce in accordance with the Prophet's practice), contrasting it with the Sunni view of *Talaq al-Bid'ah* (innovative triple divorce). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that three divorces pronounced simultaneously while the wife is in a state of purity (*al-‘Adh*) count as a single revocable divorce, whereas those pronounced during menstruation are considered ineffective (*laysa bi-shay’*), preserving the wife's status until the final count is complete.
